summary: The document describes a photocatalyst-free, visible light-mediated method for the oxidative α-C-H functionalization of tertiary amines using polyhalomethanes. The main article includes optimization tables for iminium salt formation, scope figures for various nucleophiles, and mechanistic studies including in situ IR monitoring and Kharasch-type additions.

items.heading: Scheme 1
items.caption: Iminium ions: access strategies and applications.
items.description: This scheme illustrates different strategies to access iminium ions from tertiary amines, including aerobic oxidation and the use of external oxidants like polyhalomethanes.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Transformation of THIQ 1 to its iminium salt - initial studies and reaction optimization a
items.description: Optimization of reaction conditions for the formation of iminium salt 2 from N-phenyl THIQ 1, screening light sources, equivalents of CBrCl3, and temperature.

items.heading: Fig. 1
items.caption: Visible light assisted generation of iminium ions from N -aryl and N -alkyl THIQs (yields determined by NMR using CH2Br2 or CHBr3 as internal standard).
items.description: Displays the scope of N-aryl and N-alkyl tetrahydroisoquinolines that can be converted to their corresponding iminium bromide salts.

items.heading: Fig. 2
items.caption: Cross coupling reactions of iminium bromide salts with carbon and heteroatom nucleophiles (yields determined by NMR using CH2Br2 as internal standard, isolated yields*).
items.description: Shows the scope of nucleophiles (phosphorous, carbon, and heteroatom) used in cross-coupling reactions with pregenerated iminium salts.

items.heading: Fig. 3
items.caption: Cross coupling with potassium styryl trifluoroborate (yields determined by NMR using CH2Br2 as internal standard).
items.description: Demonstrates the vinylation of THIQ and DMF derivatives using potassium styryl trifluoroborate under the developed photocatalyst-free conditions.

items.heading: Fig. 4
items.caption: In situ IR-reaction monitoring of visible light-assisted generation of THIQ iminium ion 2 from THIQ 1 with CBrCl3.
items.description: A graph showing the disappearance of THIQ starting material and the appearance of the iminium salt over time as monitored by IR spectroscopy.

items.heading: Fig. 5
items.caption: Kharasch addition of CBrCl3 with visible light.
items.description: Shows the atom transfer radical addition (ATRA) of CBrCl3 to a non-activated olefin under visible light irradiation.

items.heading: Scheme 2
items.caption: Mechanistic considerations.
items.description: Proposed mechanistic pathways including EDA complex formation, homolytic bond fission, and hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) steps.
